commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Platform] Keep PIN_MEMORY eager; avoid resolving platform during import vllm
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Reworks #60766: keeps `PIN_MEMORY` a plain eagerly-computed module global (instead of a lazy module `__getattr__` plus `is_pin_memory_available()` calls in the `torch_utils` hot paths), and fixes the underlying import-order problem instead: `import vllm` resolved `current_platform` and loaded platform plugins while vLLM was half-imported. ## Claims - `import vllm` doesn't resolve the platform (same as #60766), including with `VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG=1`, which #60766 didn't cover. - An out-of-tree platform plugin whose `register()` imports from `vllm.utils.torch_utils` is detected correctly, both for `import vllm` and `from vllm import LLM`. - `PIN_MEMORY` is a plain module global again; `async_tensor_h2d` / `np_to_pinned_tensor` read it directly. - Out-of-tree platform plugin detection failures are now logged as warnings rather than silently (debug) falling back to another platform. ## Validation Run on GB200 (CUDA), with the dummy platform plugin installed where needed: | Check | Result | |---|---| | `tests/plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py` | 4 passed | | same, `test_import_vllm_does_not_resolve_platform` with `env_override` pointed back at `torch_utils` (i.e. without the fix) | fails; new warning shows `cannot import name 'direct_register_custom_op' from partially initialized module 'vllm.utils.torch_utils'` | | `tests/test_force_first_config.py` | 3 passed | | `VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG=1`: platform resolved after `import vllm` / patch installed after `import vllm.triton_utils` / installed without env var | no / yes / no | | `tests/utils_/test_torch_utils.py` + `tests/compile/test_config.py::test_version` | 38 passed | ```bash pip install -e tests/plugins/vllm_add_dummy_platform cd tests && pytest -v plugins_tests/test_platform_plugins.py ``` Runs were on the commit before rebasing onto current main; none of the 17 intervening upstream commits touch the changed files. ## Details **Root cause.** `vllm/__init__.py` → `vllm.env_override` → `from vllm.utils.torch_utils import is_torch_equal, is_torch_equal_or_newer` → module-level `PIN_MEMORY = is_pin_memory_available()` → `current_platform` resolution → plugin `register()` runs against a partially initialized `torch_utils`. The `ImportError` was swallowed in `resolve_current_platform_cls_qualname`, so another platform was silently selected. **Changes.** - `is_torch_equal*` move to a new dependency-free `vllm/utils/torch_version.py` (re-exported from `torch_utils`, so existing imports keep working). `env_override` and `envs` import from it, so `import vllm` no longer imports `torch_utils` at all. - `PIN_MEMORY` is assigned at the end of `torch_utils.py`. Other paths (e.g. `from vllm import LLM` → `vllm.config.cache` → `torch_utils`) still resolve the platform while importing `torch_utils`; with the assignment last, a plugin importing anything else from `torch_utils` finds it already defined. The restored `test_platform_plugins` (runs `from vllm import LLM`) covers this. - The `VLLM_TRITON_FORCE_FIRST_CONFIG` autotuner patch is installed on import of `vllm.triton_utils` rather than in `env_override`, since importing that package resolves the platform. All vLLM Triton kernels import through it, so the patch is still in place before any autotuning; a third-party `triton.autotune` kernel run before `vllm.triton_utils` is imported would no longer be patched. - Plugin Integration CI step now also triggers on the files involved (it didn't run for #45424, which introduced the regression). **Not addressed (also not addressed by #60766).** `import vllm.config` still resolves the platform (`vllm/config/compilation.py` imports `current_platform` at module level), and a plugin whose `register()` needs the platform itself (e.g. imports `PIN_MEMORY` or `vllm.triton_utils`) can't work under any of these schemes. ---

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Reserve encoder graph memory without decoder graphs
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Reserve encoder CUDA graph memory during MRV2 automatic KV-cache sizing even when decoder graph mode is `NONE`. This fixes a profiling eligibility omission, not a reproduced OOM or throughput bottleneck.

While following up on [MRV2 feedback on my earlier PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54905#issuecomment-5769718464), I found a case similar to #41714 in a different runner/configuration.

## Claims

- Admit MRV2 encoder graph profiling when decoder graphs are disabled, excluding eager execution. Reuse `needs_cudagraph_capture()` in the V2 profiler instead of decoder-only eligibility checks.
- Preserve MRV1 behavior, graph-reservation opt-out semantics and existing estimation/teardown logic. No kernels, capture sizes, batch caps or pool-sharing changes.
- Reduce the reviewed diff from 150 to **62 changed lines including tests (+51/-11)** across three files. Regression coverage extends the existing profiler helper/parameterization, including pre-bootstrap initialization and cleanup on encoder capture failure.

## Validation

Tested unmodified main: `b510857d37640209a4a3e01a13260ac26f2a93f3`. Published fix: `e2edc92fd22e3f0c2ac574280d1886b65b0f05a8`; exact tested diff SHA256: `c2fc661edad37971f41312cd4b2d192477e82894fe9a59dda73bbd8ce84cd18a`.

**[Raw logs, exact commands, scripts, per-example outputs and provenance](https://gist.github.com/BWAAEEEK/176b4906758a0189cf93363e2d2060d2)**. Result tables in the review reply are verbatim tool stdout, not manually generated tables.

- B200, BF16, TP=1, Torch 2.14.0+cu130, Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct revision `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`, encoder graphs ON / decoder graphs NONE.
- Identical real-model reproducer: main captures/replays encoder graphs but reserves 0 bytes and fails the explicit accounting assertion; fixed reserves **260 MiB** and passes. The generated smoke answer matches. This is not an OOM reproduction.
- Focused suites: **110 passed**. Unmodified-main profiler negative control: **3 expected failures, 13 passed**. Separate local-only Worker mock matrix: **48 passed** fixed, **3 expected failures, 45 passed** main. ROCm/XPU are mocked, not hardware-tested.
- Full official `lm_eval` ChartQA, 2,500 examples, HTTP concurrency 8, temperature 0, output cap 512: relaxed accuracy **0.7548 main / 0.7492 fixed**. The -0.56 percentage-point difference is not hidden or treated as proven equivalent.
- Diagnostic follow-up at concurrency 1: all 54 score-changing examples plus 32 controls produced identical response texts and scores (86/86). This selected subset supports a scheduling/batch-related explanation but does not replace full-task accuracy evaluation or establish equivalence.
- Official `vllm bench serve`, real image requests, 128 measured requests + 16 warmups, concurrency 8, three rounds per variant/workload: zero failed requests in all 12 runs. Mean throughput changes were **+2.61%** for output length 1 and **-1.89%** for output length 128. Descriptive only; no general speedup or no-regression claim.
- Changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.

Focused test command (full invocation and raw output in the evidence link):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -q
```

Both variants used a fresh standard editable installation, identical dependencies and all 13 identical official CUDA extension hashes. The wheel source was `f98ae6a9fd2c73a2f80dd9fe4c534676f689394d`, not the tested main SHA. The full wheel-to-main source delta is included; no `csrc` change was present. The PR contains no C++/CUDA change.

## Details

The Worker previously gated graph memory profiling on decoder mode alone. The V2 profiler also returned early for decoder NONE or no decoder capture descriptors, even though the encoder can capture independently. This left encoder graph memory out of automatic KV-cache sizing. The fix widens eligibility without changing the memory estimator. The pre-bootstrap configuration guard remains because the decoder manager can still be uninitialized.

This is regular multimodal generation, not the separate `--mm-encoder-only` deployment mode. Reserving previously omitted graph memory can reduce the automatically selected KV-cache capacity; that is the intended accounting correction.

### Related Work / Duplicate Check

The original duplicate check covered #49224 and its comments, open issue references, and encoder graph memory/MRV2 profiling PRs. Open issue references and area searches were refreshed before this update.

- #53306 introduced the MRV2 profiler and closed #49224. This PR addresses a remaining eligibility case, not the original issue in full.
- #57865 concerns retained-workspace/released-graph accounting; #51590 concerns MRV1 capture-footprint measurement. Their accounting-policy changes remain out of scope here.
- #54061 concerns capture tracing; #56922 concerns the separate encoder-only runner.
- Merged #58430 prevents allocator fragmentation during ordinary profiling from shrinking the KV budget. This change instead fixes omitted encoder graph memory when decoder graphs are disabled. They are complementary, despite shared files.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Respect meta initialization for Engram offload
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Respect meta initialization when allocating DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram tables, preventing unnecessary host-memory allocation on encoder-only instances.

## Claims

- Skip pinned, huge-page and shared host storage during meta initialization.
- Preserve normal Engram CPU offload and suppress offload logs for meta tensors.

## Validation

Started two real-weight DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash encoder instances under Slurm using `vllm serve ... --mm-encoder-only --tensor-parallel-size 1` with Mooncake TCP. After startup, worker inspection confirmed both Engram tables remain meta with zero host-table bytes on each instance, avoiding approximately 188.8 GiB of unnecessary allocation per encoder.

## Details

Encoder-only language models are constructed under `torch.device("meta")`, but Engram explicitly allocates CPU storage. The retained language-model placeholder therefore holds two unnecessary tables, approximately 188.8 GiB per TP1 encoder instance for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.

Reuse the existing device-local allocation path before any host-storage allocation. No runner, scheduler or connector changes. Open-PR searches found no existing fix for this meta-initialization bypass.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve DP rank in Responses requests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Forward `X-data-parallel-rank` from the Responses API to the engine, matching Chat Completions. This prevents the frontend from silently discarding a gateway's selected DP replica.

## Claims

- Preserve the selected rank for streaming and non-streaming Responses requests, including subsequent built-in tool turns.
- Keep existing default routing when the header is absent or cannot be parsed; rank zero is preserved.

## Validation

On upstream base `fb61ac07bd1d5b8b9722c80085b99ef770efb265`, Python 3.12.13, CPU platform with accelerator visibility disabled:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu VLLM_PLUGINS='' ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES='' \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py \
  -k 'responses_data_parallel_rank or harmony_tool_followup_preserves_render_params' -v -ra --tb=short
```

Result: **11 passed, 66 deselected**, no skips. Tests exercise header parsing through the Responses serving entrypoint to `engine.generate`, and reuse the existing tool-follow-up test. They are included in the existing Buildkite Responses test area.

Serving reproduction on an Ascend-native downstream deployment with a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model, Mooncake PD, prefill TP4/DP4 and decode TP8/DP2:

| Request | Before forwarding | After forwarding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same reconstructed streaming Responses request, reasoning effort `max`, approximately 7.1k prompt tokens | No generated output within 45 seconds; decode waiting for KV fetch | Completed in approximately 3 seconds, including text and `response.completed` |

The serving comparison used a runtime implementation of the same rank-forwarding change on prefill API processes, without restarting the model. It validates the routing correction on that deployment; it is not a deployment of this exact upstream commit. The original client tool schemas were unavailable, so this was a reconstructed reproducer, not a byte-identical replay. No accuracy benchmark or general performance improvement is claimed.

## Details

The gateway can select prefill replica R and direct decode to fetch KV from R. Responses previously omitted `data_parallel_rank` from its engine call, allowing internal load balancing to choose another replica. Decode can then wait for KV at the wrong producer. The fix uses the existing header parser and passes the rank explicitly through `_generate_with_builtin_tools` to every `engine.generate` call. No connector-specific behavior or hardware branch is added.

Duplicate-work checks found no existing PR for this fix. Related #40285 changes internal DP coordinator notifications, and #49246 adds PCP/DP support; neither changes Responses rank forwarding.

AI assistance was used to investigate, implement, and test this change.

commits.pr_title: [Benchmark] Add steady-state PP support to bench forward
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Add pipeline parallelism to `vllm bench forward`, measuring a microbatch's full-pipeline forward latency under steady-state load from identical microbatches. Builds on the merged PCP support in #63613. ## Claims - Includes PP transfers and waits between the first stage's forward start and the last stage's forward completion; excludes pipeline fill/drain, input preparation before the forward, and sampling. - Captures each stage's forward in a CUDA graph and streams matching microbatches without a per-step host barrier. Reports stage timelines and estimated cross-rank clock uncertainty. - Adds rendered CLI documentation and a two-GPU CLI/profiler regression test wired into the existing distributed CI job. ## Validation Full 93-layer Kimi K3 with dummy MXFP4 weights on **4 nodes × 4 GB200 GPUs**. Balanced routing, 8,192 query tokens per microbatch, EP enabled. PP2 uses TP8/EP8; PP4 uses TP4/EP4. Kimi currently disables SP with PP. Median full-pipeline GPU latency (ms): | PP | Prefill | TRT-LLM bench | TRT-LLM serving | MegaMoE bench | MegaMoE serving | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 2 | 8 × 1K | 338.3 | 339.3 | 525.4 | 525.8 | | 2 | 1 × 8K | 357.1 | 357.9 | 517.6 | 518.1 | | 4 | 8 × 1K | 490.7 | 491.6 | 645.7 | 646.9 | | 4 | 1 × 8K | 507.3 | 505.5 | 637.8 | 637.2 | Serving measurements match request IDs across stages and use the same first/last GPU-event boundaries; these are not TTFT or Prometheus prefill histogram values. Serving uses piecewise graphs. All differences are within 0.35%. Benchmark-only KV restoration is outside stage compute timing but can affect pipeline cadence. Each benchmark case has 100 measured microbatches (5 × 20), trimming 4 × PP microbatches at each end. Final-run sample-median spread was below 1%; estimated cross-rank clock uncertainty was about 0.18–0.21 ms. All intermediate and final benchmark outputs were finite and matched the eager pipeline reference exactly. These dummy-weight checks validate execution and timing, not model quality. Both MoE backends use MXFP8 × MXFP4. MegaMoE's additional cost here includes replicated token dispatch with SP disabled; this PR does not change the model or MoE implementation.
Commands and regression evidence Full CLI suite before the final aggregation/profiling cleanup: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py -v # 9 passed .venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \ .buildkite/test_areas/distributed.yaml docs/cli/README.md docs/benchmarking/cli.md \ tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py vllm/benchmarks/forward/main.py \ vllm/benchmarks/forward/pipeline.py # All applicable hooks passed ``` After the cleanup, reran the real two-GPU CLI/profiler test: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py::test_bench_forward_pipeline -v # 1 passed ``` The CPU aggregation reproduces all 100 saved latency samples exactly for each of the eight Kimi/backend/layout/shape cases. Final pre-commit checks also pass. The cleanup removes a redundant GPU reduction after gathering timelines, skips clock calibration and timing events in the profiling pass, and removes duplicate checks; the timed transfers and graph replay order are unchanged. Before the implementation, the new test was copied into an isolated worktree at `dbbb4f73de` (PCP branch tip) and run there with the same environment: ```bash PYTHONPATH=/tmp/vllm-forward-pp-base \ /home/woosuk/workspace/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py::test_bench_forward_pipeline -v # FAILED: Value error, Model Runner V2 does not yet support: # pipeline parallelism with external_launcher ``` Benchmark command, run on each node (set `PP=2` or `4`, and the torchrun rendezvous variables): ```bash VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip .venv/bin/torchrun \ --nnodes=4 --nproc-per-node=4 --node-rank="$NODE_RANK" \ --master-addr="$MASTER_ADDR" --master-port=29641 \ -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \ --model moonshotai/Kimi-K3 --trust-remote-code --load-format dummy \ --pipeline-parallel-size "$PP" --tensor-parallel-size "$((16 / PP))" \ --enable-expert-parallel --max-model-len 9216 \ --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 8 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune false \ --routing balanced --kv-len-jitter 0 \ --case 'prefill8x1k=8*1024' --case prefill1x8k=8192 \ --iters 20 --samples 5 --output-json results.json ``` For MegaMoE, add `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`. Model config/tokenizer revision: `f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06`. Serving used the same layouts, model, routing fixture and input tokens, with prefix caching and FlashInfer autotuning disabled, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`, `max_num_seqs=16*PP`, and `{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[8192]}`. A diagnostic worker recorded CUDA events around real stage forwards, without per-step synchronization. The client sent 100 groups of eight 1K requests, then 100 8K requests, all with one output token; analysis selected exact-shape microbatches and discarded fill/drain. Backend class and precision were checked on all 16 ranks for MegaMoE.
## Details The implementation is isolated to the benchmark. A benchmark-specific external-launcher executor enables stage loading; the benchmark drives the runners directly, without serving schedulers or sampling broadcasts. It reuses runner input preparation, forward context, KV-state handling, and PP/TP transfer conventions. Cross-device CUDA events cannot be subtracted directly. Pre/post calibration correlates each GPU's timeline to rank zero's monotonic clock using CPU ping-pong and host/GPU event bracketing. The benchmark reports the earliest first-stage TP start to latest last-stage TP completion for each microbatch, with the calibration uncertainty retained in JSON. This adds code compared with timing isolated stages, but is needed to measure pipeline traversal while other stages remain occupied. The full-model validation covers prefill with PP+TP+EP. Decode and combinations with PCP/DCP are not covered by these full-model runs. No serving/model code or non-PP benchmark behavior is changed. Duplicate check: searched open PRs for `"bench forward"`, pipeline benchmarking, PCP/PP benchmarking, and references to #63613. No open PR implements this feature. #62300 fixes profiling in the existing forward path and is separate from PP support. AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and this description. Human review of the final diff remains required before marking the draft ready. ---

commits.pr_title: [Benchmark] Add PCP support to vllm bench forward
commits.pr_body:
## Overview Add prefill context parallelism (PCP) support to `vllm bench forward`, including PCP with expert parallelism and decode context parallelism. ## Claims - Validate requested batch shapes against the global batch and inject the correct token slices into each rank's split or replicated request rows. - Account for PCP workers in balanced MoE routing fixtures and report local batch sizes/order in per-rank results. - Document PCP usage and the distinction between full-forward graph timing and serving latency. ## Validation - Seven CPU tests passed in `tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py` (all tests except the existing single-GPU model test). The new two-rank parameterized regression checks split prefill slices with a continued prefix, replicated decode inputs, and untouched padding. This file runs in the existing Benchmarks CLI Buildkite job. - All pre-commit hooks passed on the four changed files. - Before the change, the four-GPU CLI reproducer fails in `_check_batch` with `AssertionError: ['bench-0', 'bench-0']`. With the change, uneven prefill, mixed prefill/decode, and decode cases complete. - On four GB200 GPUs, GLM-5.2 NVFP4 with dummy weights was exercised with PCP4/EP4, PCP2/TP2/EP4, and PCP2/TP2/DCP2/EP4. DCP used `ag_rs`, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, and `fp8_ds_mla`. Real and balanced synthetic routing were exercised; full-model timing was compared with `vllm serve`. - Real `nvidia/GLM-5.3-NVFP4` weights were also tested with PCP4/EP4, normal routing, and both TRTLLM and NVFP4 MegaMoE backends: | MoE backend | Prompt tokens | Forward graph (ms) | Serving TTFT (ms) | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `flashinfer_trtllm` | 1,024 | 50.708 | 94.067 | | `flashinfer_trtllm` | 8,192 | 163.816 | 174.005 | | `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` | 1,024 | 58.483 | 95.870 | | `flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl` | 8,192 | 153.638 | 160.496 | These are functionality/timing checks, not speedup claims for the patch. Forward timing used 10 replays × 3 samples; MegaMoE sample spread was 0.14% / 0.49% for 1K / 8K. TTFT is the median of 10 serial requests after four warmups. Both paths used identical README-derived prompt IDs, disabled FlashInfer autotuning, and real routing; serving used `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, while the benchmark captures the full forward. Kernel traces confirmed the selected MoE implementations. Outputs were finite. The real-weight 1K graph/eager comparison was exact; the 8K case showed variability even between eager repeats, so these results do **not** establish 8K numerical parity or task-level accuracy. No inference/model implementation is changed.
Reproduction commands ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py \ -k 'not test_bench_forward' -q .venv/bin/python -m pytest \ tests/benchmarks/test_forward_cli.py::test_bench_forward_rejects_oversized_verify -q # Four-layer functional smoke; MODEL is a local GLM-5.2 NVFP4 config/tokenizer. .venv/bin/torchrun --nproc-per-node=4 -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench forward \ --model "$MODEL" --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers":4}' \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 \ --enable-expert-parallel --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune false \ --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --max-num-seqs 4 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 --kv-len-jitter 0 \ --case uneven=1025 --case mix=513@2048c,3*1@2048 --case decode=4*1@2048 \ --iters 3 --samples 2 --output-json /tmp/forward-pcp-smoke.json ``` The performance table comes from the earlier full-model experiments in this work, rather than the reduced-layer smoke command above.
## Details PCP can represent one global request with two disjoint local rows. Previously the benchmark required unique local request IDs and copied the entire query for every row. It now checks the global batch contract and derives each local token slice from its computed-token offset and scheduled-token count. Balanced routing includes PCP in the EP world size and reserves capacity for gathered PCP rows without EP. Duplicate-work checks found no open PCP/forward benchmark PR or matching issue. #62300 addresses CUPTI profiling and is separate from this change. No issue number was supplied. AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and PR preparation. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Preserve FP8 indexer WK pairs across load_weights calls
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

**In short**: Bugfix for GLM-5.3 sometimes starting with degraded performance (thinking loops) due to dropped weights when using runai_streamer loader due to a "race" (non-deterministic I/O completion order).

**Details**:
GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek-V3.2 (`deepseek_v32`) checkpoints store the indexer `wk` projection in FP8 as two tensors: values and a scale factor. The loader parks the first half in a dict and dequantizes once the second half arrives, but that dict was created fresh on every `load_weights()` call, so the two halves had to arrive within the same call.
 
With runai_streamer as loader, tensors arrive in IO-completion order (this is partly the cause for the non-deterministic "race"), and `AutoWeightsLoader` splits the weight stream into multiple `load_weights()` calls at every `model` <-> `lm_head` prefix transition. When the split between calls happens to fall between the two halves of a pair, both are silently dropped: the WK half of the fused `wk_weights_proj` parameter keeps its initialization, one layer's sparse-attention indexer runs on garbage, and every load-completeness check still passes. In production this shows up as a per-launch coin flip where short answers look fine but long reasoning degenerates into thinking loops, rendering the performance almost useless.

Fix: keep the pending dict on the model instance instead of a local variable (similar fix as #46168 for the generic `deepseek_v2` path, applied to the remaining copies: `deepseek_v32` nvidia/amd model+mtp, and `deepseek_mtp`).

Note that this is NOT a duplicate of #56584, which fixes the `glm5next` (GLM-5.3-Flash) copy of the same bug. The two PRs touch disjoint files and both are needed.

## Test Plan

```bash
     .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_deepseek_v32_weight_loading.py -v
```

That test is CPU-only, no GPU and no checkpoint needed.

## Test Result

* Unpatched main: 13 failed (the WK half of the fused parameter stays all-zero, which is the bug addressed in this PR)
* With this PR: 13 passed.

Also verified end-to-end on a real GLM-5.3 deployment (TP=8, B200, --load-format runai_streamer). In addition to checking by hand with complex prompts that force the model to do multi-thinking steps and therefore validating that the thinking loops were gone, the following checks were done (with help of AI):
* Dumped the live in-VRAM wk_weights_proj tensors from all 8 TP workers and compared them bitwise against values dequantized from the on-disk checkpoint: 168/168 identical.
* 10 greedy prompts (math / code / instructions): content and reasoning byte-identical to a known-good instance of the same weights, so a healthy load is provably unchanged and accuracy benchmarks are unaffected.

No documentation update is needed.
AI assistance was used to help investigate, implement, and test this change.

## Overview

Clef builds and copies several small metadata tensors for every request. This uses NumPy for the CPU work and reduces the pooler’s host-to-device copies from nine to three per request, leaving the decision-head math unchanged.

## Validation

Model: [Cloudflare/clef-flash](https://huggingface.co/Cloudflare/clef-flash), BF16, MRV2, native `/v1/systemone`. All pairs below are **main → PR**; C means concurrent requests, and input tokens are rounded means.

**B300:** measured roughly 3–5% higher throughput on the tested short, single-question workloads; longer inputs were effectively flat. The controlled study and profiling details below qualify that result.

| C | Input tokens / questions | Requests/s | Throughput change | p50 latency (ms) | p99 latency (ms) | Peak device memory (MiB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 209 / 1 | 114.58 → 118.30 | +3.25% | 69.61 → 67.51 | 72.75 → 69.59 | 83,370 → 83,370 |
| 16 | 209 / 1 | 163.61 → 168.18 | +2.79% | 97.49 → 94.94 | 102.26 → 98.57 | 83,778 → 83,778 |
| 32 | 209 / 1 | 185.17 → 191.25 | +3.28% | 172.24 → 167.51 | 190.32 → 184.20 | 84,562 → 84,562 |
| 64 | 209 / 1 | 200.12 → 205.82 | +2.85% | 318.54 → 310.17 | 334.01 → 315.42 | 85,458 → 85,094 |
| 16 | 986 / 8 | 79.85 → 79.94 | +0.11% | 200.07 → 199.88 | 205.75 → 204.44 | 86,502 → 86,486 |
| 8 | 4946 / 32 | 17.04 → 17.05 | +0.04% | 391.45 → 391.66 | 587.15 → 587.05 | 87,656 → 87,640 |

The reference test passed on both versions, 306 CPU + 306 GPU metadata cases matched across four streams, and all 1,024 question results matched main versus PR within serial/C16 modes. Another 112 requests passed with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on B300. Timed requests for the displayed cases: **93,272 on B300, zero errors**. These checks establish output parity, not labeled task accuracy.

<details>
<summary>Controlled input-length study (B300)</summary>

This separate C16 study fixes three options per question and verifies the total input-token count on every response. Each version used two fresh servers in main → PR → PR → main order, with two 30-second windows per case/server after 10 seconds of warmup. The last two servers reversed case order. Profiling was disabled.

| Input tokens / questions | Requests/s, main → PR | Change | p50 / p99 latency (ms), main → PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 256 / 1 | 155.27 → 162.48 | +4.64% | 102.78 / 107.39 → 97.72 / 104.98 |
| 1,024 / 1 | 79.65 → 79.80 | +0.19% | 200.65 / 208.20 → 200.14 / 208.16 |
| 4,096 / 1 | 22.75 → 22.78 | +0.11% | 703.03 / 756.60 → 702.19 / 743.61 |
| 4,096 / 8 | 22.30 → 22.36 | +0.29% | 717.10 / 775.72 → 715.19 / 775.09 |
| 4,096 / 32 | 21.33 → 21.39 | +0.24% | 749.04 / 776.80 → 747.32 / 761.79 |

With one question, the serving gain becomes effectively flat as input length increases. At 4,096 tokens, changing question count from 1 to 8 to 32 also leaves serving throughput effectively flat; the isolated B16 pooler still improves by 3.0%, 4.6% and 8.5%, respectively. Those pooler timings use real head weights with synthetic hidden states and lexical embeddings.

The short-input mean is variable: main windows ranged from 154.18–155.95 requests/s and PR windows from 156.86–172.07; +4.64% is an observed average, not a guaranteed gain. There were 73,659 timed requests with zero errors and 344 exactly matching question results in separate parity checks. Peak sampled whole-device/process memory was 93,462/92,510 MiB on both versions; these include KV cache and retained allocations.

This study uses `--max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 65536`, allowing C16 × 4,096 tokens without the original table’s token-budget limit. The other model, dtype, affinity and prefix-cache settings are unchanged. More questions replace state padding and increase total options; this separates total length from question count, not question overhead from option overhead. Both arms use the same existing source/wheel environment with the exact baseline/PR pooler methods applied, not separate current-main rebuilds.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Focused CPU/GPU profile (B300)</summary>

Nsight Systems captured warmed-up Q1/C16 requests at 256 and 1,024 total tokens, with temporary NVTX markers around schema parsing, indices, transfers, head execution and frontend encoding. Four fresh servers supplied one accepted three-second capture per variant/length: 1,207 requests, zero errors. Capture head counts match client completions; eight separate paired requests matched exactly.

| Input tokens | Profiled `_indices` host duration/request, main → PR | Pooler H2D copies/request | Head kernels/request |
|---|---|---|---|
| 256 | 0.366 → 0.197 ms | 9 → 3 | 179 → 179 |
| 1,024 | 0.514 → 0.212 ms | 9 → 3 | 185 → 185 |

Bytes transferred remain 779/request for these inputs. GPU activity overlaps about 31–37% of the pooler host span at 256 tokens and 77–82% at 1,024 tokens. This supports CPU/GPU overlap as an explanation, but profiling perturbs timing and batch formation, so it does not attribute the full unprofiled throughput gain. These are instrumented host spans, not CPU time saved on the critical path.

For short inputs, the head still occupies about 88% of the PR pooler’s host span, including kernel dispatch; frontend encoding is about 0.60 ms/request on both versions. Other frontend costs are not conclusively attributed. Any head-batching experiment belongs in a separate PR.

Capture configuration: CUDA/NVTX/OS-runtime tracing, 100 Hz Python sampling, CUDA graph tracing at graph granularity, 15 seconds of warmup, then a three-second capture started/stopped through the native profiling endpoints. No profiler timings are used in the serving tables. Nsight lost its agent on later captures; only complete first captures from verified fresh servers were retained and checked against client counts.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Methodology, reproduction and test commands</summary>

**Reproducer:** start a fresh server for each arm, selecting its source tree on `PYTHONPATH`. B300 used GPU 0, server CPUs 0–15, client CPUs 16–19 and `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.3`:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
  PYTHONPATH=/path/to/base-or-branch \
  taskset -c 0-15 .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /path/to/clef-flash \
  --served-model-name clef --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 8192 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 18971 --seed 0

taskset -c 16-19 .venv/bin/python bench_confirm.py --label main-A --duration 15 --rounds 2
```
The client warms up each case with `max(C, 8)` requests, includes draining outstanding requests in elapsed time, and samples memory/clocks every 0.5 seconds. `vllm bench serve` had no native SystemOne adapter in the tested versions. Save as `bench_confirm.py`:

    if args.profile: cases=[(1,64,1),(16,64,1),(16,256,8)]
    report={'label':args.label,'duration_per_round_s':args.duration,'cases':[]}
    timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=120)
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(timeout=timeout,connector=aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=96)) as session:
        async def call(body):
            started=time.perf_counter()
            async with session.post(url+'/v1/systemone',json=body) as response:
                data=await response.json()
                if response.status!=200: raise RuntimeError((response.status,data))
            return (time.perf_counter()-started)*1000,data
        for concurrency,words,questions in cases:
            bodies=[request(i,words,questions) for i in range(max(128,concurrency*2))]
            await asyncio.gather(*(call(bodies[i%len(bodies)]) for i in range(max(concurrency,8))))
            if args.profile:
                async with session.post(url+'/start_profile',json={'profile_prefix':f'C{concurrency}W{words}Q{questions}','max_iterations':8}) as r:
                    if r.status!=200: raise RuntimeError(await r.text())
            rounds=[]
            for ri in range(args.rounds):
                started=time.perf_counter()
                latencies=[]; usages=[]; samples=[]; errors=[]
                monitoring=True
                memory_samples=[]
                async def monitor():
                    while monitoring:
                        info=pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetMemoryInfo(gpu)
                        memory_samples.append({'at_s':time.perf_counter()-started,
                            'device_used_mib':info.used/1048576,
                            'gpu_utilization':pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetUtilizationRates(gpu).gpu,
                            'temperature_c':pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetTemperature(gpu,pynvml.NVML_TEMPERATURE_GPU),
                            'sm_clock_mhz':pynvml.nvmlDeviceGetClockInfo(gpu,pynvml.NVML_CLOCK_SM),
                            'cpu_server_affinity_percent':psutil.cpu_percent(interval=None,percpu=True)[:16]})
                        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
                monitor_task=asyncio.create_task(monitor())
                async def worker(w):
                    i=w
                    while time.perf_counter()-started<args.duration:
                        try:
                            latency,data=await call(bodies[i%len(bodies)])
                            latencies.append(latency);usages.append(data['usage']['input_tokens'])
                            if len(samples)<8: samples.append({'body':bodies[i%len(bodies)],'response':data})
                        except Exception as e:
                            errors.append(str(e))
                            break
                        i+=concurrency
                await asyncio.gather(*(worker(w) for w in range(concurrency)))
                elapsed=time.perf_counter()-started
                monitoring=False
                await monitor_task
                if not latencies: raise RuntimeError(errors)
                row={'concurrency':concurrency,'state_words':words,'questions':questions,'round':ri,
                     'requests':len(latencies),'errors':errors,'elapsed_s':elapsed,
                     'requests_per_s':len(latencies)/elapsed,'questions_per_s':len(latencies)*questions/elapsed,
                     'p50_ms':percentile(latencies,50),'p99_ms':percentile(latencies,99),
                     'mean_input_tokens':statistics.mean(usages),'latencies_ms':latencies,'samples':samples,
                     'device_memory_peak_mib':max(x['device_used_mib'] for x in memory_samples),
                     'monitor_samples':memory_samples}
                rounds.append(row)
                print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in row.items() if k not in ('samples','latencies_ms','monitor_samples')}),flush=True)
            if args.profile:
                async with session.post(url+'/stop_profile') as r:
                    if r.status!=200: raise RuntimeError(await r.text())
            report['cases'].extend(rounds)
            (ROOT/f'serving-{args.label}.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__': asyncio.run(main())

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Core] Keep scheduling running requests after a priority self-preemption
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Under `--scheduling-policy priority`, when a running request cannot get KV blocks the scheduler preempts the lowest-priority running request. `self.running` is in admission order, not priority order, so that request can sit in the middle of the list, for example when higher-priority requests arrived after it. If it is the request currently being scheduled, it preempts itself, and the running loop then `break`s:

```python
if new_blocks is None:
    # Cannot schedule this request.
    break
```

Every running request after it gets no tokens in that step, even though they all have higher priority, the self-preemption just freed blocks, and budget remains. This is a priority inversion: the requests the policy is meant to protect lose a step whenever a lower-priority request ahead of them runs out of KV.

After a self-preemption the request has already been removed from `self.running` (`del self.running[victim_index]` with `victim_index == req_index`), so `req_index` already points at the next request. The fix continues the loop in that case. Nothing changes for FCFS: it preempts `running[-1]`, so a self-preemption there only happens on the last request. Other reasons for a failed allocation (a deferred free that will not help, pending connector frees) still end the loop.

Related but different: #49097 (fixed by #49206) adjusted `req_index` when the victim sits before the cursor. #39375, a larger rework of this preemption path that has been open since March, would also remove this `break`.

## Test Plan

- New `test_priority_self_preemption_keeps_scheduling_later_running_requests`. Setup: one free block, `running = [A(p0), B(p5), C(p0)]`; A and B both need a new block on the same decode step, C does not. A takes the block, B preempts itself, and C must still be scheduled.
- `tests/v1/core` in full, main vs this PR.
- A random-workload stall check on the real `Scheduler` (small per-step budgets, priority/FCFS mixed, hybrid attention+Mamba and full-attention layouts, 40 seeds each). It flags a running request that gets 0 tokens while the step has budget left for its whole remainder; this is how I found it.

## Test Result

(CPU only.)

- New test: fails on main (`{'A': 1}` scheduled, C skipped), passes with this PR.
- `tests/v1/core` in full: same failed/errored set on main `fa75d3456d` and on this PR (68 environment failures on both trees, e.g. missing `torchvision` and offline model configs); 0 failures only on this PR; 953 → 954 passed (the new test).
- Stall check, hybrid layout: main stalls on 1/40 seeds (this bug), this PR on 0/40. Full-attention layout: 0/40 on both, with identical per-run action counts. A KV-content check over 60 more seeds on this PR found nothing.
- `pre-commit run --files <changed files>`: all hooks pass.
